clue.text: Drink with the mob and black out

parts.note: to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls
the press is a crowd or throng, a mob of people pushing together

explanation.surface: A night of boozing with gangsters that ends in someone losing consciousness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black out' looks like fainting, but here it means censoring or hushing something up.
explanation.definitionFit: To black out news is to censor it, keeping it hidden from the public.

clue.text: Initiate display

definitions.meaning: to start or trigger something, such as an alarm or a chain of events
to show to good effect, as a frame enhances a picture

explanation.surface: Two words suggesting the launch of an exhibition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both triggering something and showing something off to advantage.

clue.text: Cope with freak distribution giving nothing away

indicators.note: distribution spreads things about, so the letters of the two words are dealt out anew

explanation.surface: Handling a strange share-out of cards without betraying any emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distribution' suggests dealing cards, which suits the poker theme.
explanation.definitionFit: An expressionless face reveals none of one's thoughts, like a card player hiding a hand.

clue.text: Soldier qualified for overhaul

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are British army soldiers
fit means suitable or qualified for a task

explanation.surface: A soldier deemed suitable to be given a complete check-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A refit is a renovation, a thorough overhaul of a ship or building.

clue.text: Active ethnic group in Senegal is Arab

indicators.note: one piece set in another goes inside it

parts.note: SN is the country code for Senegal
A is the grammatical abbreviation for active
a race is an ethnic group

explanation.surface: A statement about which ethnic group is most active in Senegal.
explanation.definitionFit: Saracen was the medieval European name for an Arab or Muslim.

clue.text: Ceases to be interrupted by Romeo's fits of temper

indicators.note: something interrupted has another thing break into its middle, so the word for ceasing is split open

parts.note: ceases means stops
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Romeo's tantrums cut short whenever someone stops him, a Shakespearean lover's moods.
explanation.definitionFit: Strops are sulks or tantrums in informal British speech.

clue.text: Team leader supervised recreation in ecstasy

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to run a business is to supervise it
sport is recreation or play

explanation.surface: A captain overseeing games while high on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ecstasy' looks like the drug but means rapture.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in transports of joy is to be carried away by overwhelming delight.

clue.text: Excessive hesitation of fish- eater

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means excessive
er is the sound of hesitation in speech

explanation.surface: Too much dithering by someone deciding on seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: The river mammal lives largely on fish caught in streams.

clue.text: School head has sycophant who writes badly

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a crawler is a toady who sucks up to superiors

explanation.surface: A headmaster with a toady who has terrible handwriting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School head' looks like a headteacher; it is the first letter of 'School'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who scrawls produces untidy, illegible handwriting.

clue.text: Catch kite and fear breakage

indicators.note: a breakage smashes the words kite and fear apart so their letters can be reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone flying a kite worried it will snap and be lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Wood that catches begins to burn, which is the idiom for starting to blaze.

clue.text: Henry gets change of riding gear

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
to change something is to alter it

explanation.surface: A rider called Henry swaps his equestrian kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A halter is the rope or strap headgear used to lead or tie a horse, part of a rider's tack.

clue.text: A group of subjects found in retirement in Australia

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the letters are read backwards
the letters sit in the word Australia

explanation.surface: A university course list discovered by a pensioner living Down Under.
explanation.definitionFit: The humanities taught at a university are collectively called this, as opposed to sciences.

clue.text: Trees take time to become predominant

parts.note: firs are coniferous trees

explanation.surface: Saplings slowly growing over the years until they dominate the forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something predominant is foremost or leading, ranking ahead of all others.

clue.text: Irish port's sailors use this to get to the drink

definitions.text: use this to get to the drink

parts.note: Cork is a port city in the south of Ireland
a ship's crew are its sailors

explanation.surface: Sailors in Cork harbour finding a way to reach the sea, the drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The drink' is slang for the sea, which fits the sailors, but the definition means wine in a corked bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A corkscrew is the tool for pulling the stopper so you can pour wine.

clue.text: Will infect

definitions.meaning: to will something is to bequeath it to an heir
to infect someone is to transmit a disease to them

explanation.surface: Two bare words, a legal document and a disease.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers both handing property down to heirs and transmitting an illness to another person.

clue.text: Son has convulsions seeing carnage

parts.note: convulsions of mirth are fits of laughter

explanation.surface: A boy in fits as he watches a bloodbath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convulsions' suggests seizures; here it means helpless laughing.
explanation.definitionFit: Carnage is wholesale killing, a massacre.

clue.text: Cat plague

definitions.meaning: a ... in the sense of an affliction or curse

explanation.surface: Two bare words suggesting a feline disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cat' is the whip used for flogging, not an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A whip for flogging and a widespread affliction are both senses of the same noun.

clue.text: Copy for spin doctor entering contract

indicators.note: one piece entering another goes inside it

parts.note: to contract is to shrink or reduce
a PRO is a public relations officer, a spin doctor

explanation.surface: Duplicating a document for a press adviser joining under a new deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' looks like a noun, a deal; it is the verb meaning shrink.
explanation.definitionFit: To reproduce is to make a copy or replica of something.

clue.text: Doctor the girls' sweet treat

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
lasses are girls

explanation.surface: A medic tampering with the young women's dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a verb meaning tamper with; it is the noun MO.
explanation.definitionFit: The thick dark syrup from sugar refining is used to sweeten treats like toffee.

clue.text: Lovebird's to display outdoors

parts.note: love is O, the zero score in tennis, and a pen is a female swan
to air opinions or clothes is to display them

explanation.surface: A lovebird about to show off its plumage outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lovebird' must be split into love (O) and bird (PEN).
explanation.definitionFit: Taking place outside rather than under a roof, as in an alfresco concert.

clue.text: Loudly scold scoundrel without the last bit of contrition

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the scoundrel word goes round the letter

parts.note: a rat is a scoundrel or traitor

indicators.note: the last bit of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Telling off a rogue who shows no remorse at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like lacking; it means outside, around.
explanation.definitionFit: To rant is to rail or shout angrily at length.

clue.text: Recorded somebody catching bug

indicators.note: one word catching another holds it inside, as a net holds a catch

parts.note: somebody means some one person
a tap is a listening device fitted to a phone, a bug

explanation.surface: Someone captured on film catching an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Captured on a recording medium, so the words or sounds are preserved for playback.

clue.text: Perform works by Lawrence

parts.note: opera is Latin plural of opus, meaning works
T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, is known by his initials TE

explanation.surface: Staging some compositions by the author D. H. or T. E. Lawrence.
explanation.definitionFit: To operate a machine is to work it, to make it perform its function.

clue.text: Passionate earl in dance of death

indicators.note: one piece set in another goes inside it
a dance moves the letters of death around into a new order

explanation.surface: A nobleman taking part in a macabre danse macabre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dance of' turns DEATH into HATED, and E goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A heated argument is fiery and full of strong emotion.

clue.text: Boasting of exotic orange car

indicators.note: exotic means strange or foreign, so the letters are made unfamiliar by rearrangement

explanation.surface: Showing off with a flashy orange sports car.
explanation.definitionFit: Boasting is a show of excessive pride, which is haughty self-importance.

clue.text: Criticise a society involved in corruption

indicators.note: being involved in something puts a piece inside it

parts.note: rot is decay or moral corruption

explanation.surface: Condemning a club caught up in a bribery scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast someone is to criticise or ridicule them severely.

clue.text: Promiscuous sweetheart is after the toilets

indicators.note: one piece being after another places it later in the answer

parts.note: loo is British slang for a toilet

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter

explanation.surface: A lover chasing someone towards the public conveniences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetheart' must be split: the heart of 'sweet' is its middle letter E.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose is a dated term for someone of lax sexual morals.

clue.text: Surrender the French way

parts.note: le is the French masculine word for the
Ave, avenue, is a way or street

explanation.surface: Giving in, as the French supposedly do.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave something is to abandon or give it up, relinquishing it.

clue.text: Inadequate lavatory in filthy place

indicators.note: one piece set in another goes inside it

parts.note: a pigsty or sty is the byword for a filthy place
can is American slang for a lavatory

explanation.surface: A grim review of the toilet facilities in a squalid dump.
explanation.definitionFit: Scanty means meagre, barely enough, too little for the need.

clue.text: Factor storing water and weedkiller

indicators.note: a container storing something holds it within, so the word for factor encloses the water

parts.note: a factor is a part or element of something
aqua is Latin for water

explanation.surface: A farm agent keeping a supply of water and herbicide.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraquat is a toxic herbicide widely sprayed on weeds.

clue.text: Father accepts a time for parody

indicators.note: something that accepts another takes it in, so the father word holds the other letters

parts.note: to sire is to father, and a sire is a father

explanation.surface: Dad agrees to let some time go to a comic send-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are forms of mockery that ridicule by exaggerated imitation.

clue.text: Republican always gets motive of clergyman

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful
an end is an aim or purpose, the motive for acting

explanation.surface: A Republican politician always finds a reason to bring in a priest.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverend is the title and informal term for a member of the clergy.
